newsitem.title: USA: Perry dismisses idea of U.S. patrols in Hebron.
newsitem.headline: Perry dismisses idea of U.S. patrols in Hebron.

text.p: Defence Secretary William Perry said Tuesday no international force including U.S. troops to patrol the West Bank city of Hebron was being considered to resolve Israeli-Palestinian differences.
"It is not under active consideration," Perry said before meeting Israeli Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai.

Perry made the comment when told Palestinian authorities had suggested the dispute over Hebron be resolved by having an international force including U.S. troops safeguard the 400 Jewish settlers who live there in heavily-armed compounds.
Palestinian President Yasser Arafat said on Tuesday he was ready to have U.S. troops guard Jewish settlers in Hebron if that would calm Israeli security fears.
Israel agreed last year to pull back its troops in the city of 100,000 Palestinians but Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said he wanted changes to safeguard the Jewish settlers.

Mordechai made no comment on the idea of an international force but said: "I hope in a very short time we will have agreement with the Palestinian authority and when we have agreement in very short time we can redeploy in Hebron."
